content.text:
I fixed the fiscal calendar in `fiscal/calendar.py`. All 18 tests now pass; 8 were failing before.

**What was wrong:**

| Bug | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `_nearest_saturday` only ever stepped back to the previous Saturday | The year never ended in early February, so those days were counted in the next fiscal year. FY2024 ended Jan 25, 2025 instead of Feb 1, 2025. Because some year ends were off, the years with 53 weeks were wrong too. | It now picks the Saturday within 3 days of Jan 31, earlier or later: `d + timedelta(days=(5 - d.weekday() + 3) % 7 - 3)` |
| In `_period_lengths`, the extra week went into `lengths[0]` | In 53-week years, period 1 had 5 weeks instead of period 12, which SPEC §4 requires | Changed to `lengths[-1] += 1` |

**Check:**
```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
Ran 18 tests in 0.001s
OK
```
Between 2015 and 2030, the 53-week years are now FY2017, FY2023 and FY2028. Each one ends Feb 3 of the following year. This matches the standard retail 4-5-4 calendar's 53-week years.

Only `fiscal/calendar.py` changed (3 lines), and I haven't committed it.
